title: Google Review NFC Cards — NTAG213 + GBP Tap-to-Review + FTC 16 CFR Part 465 Programme Guide
summary: A tap-to-review NFC card removes the single biggest friction point in getting Google reviews from satisfied customers: the steps between intent and action. This guide covers how to select, program and deploy Google review NFC cards (NTAG213 NFC chip + custom-printed PVC body + rewritable NDEF URI record carrying the Google Business Profile short-review link) for restaurants, clinics, salons, hotels, gyms, retail counters and any business where in-person review prompts generate the most reliable results — operated within FTC 16 CFR Part 465 Rule on the Use of Consumer Reviews and Testimonials, FTC Endorsement Guides and Google Business Profile review policies (no review-gating, no incentivised reviews).
heroPoints: No app download needed. A tap opens the Google review page directly on any modern iPhone or Android.
Review volume increases of 40–70% are reported by businesses switching from verbal prompts to tap cards.
Rewritable NFC URL means one card batch can be redirected to any review platform without reprinting.

brief.label: What to confirm before ordering
items: Confirm your Google Business Profile review link is live and correct before programming cards.
Decide whether the URL should be rewritable (for future redirect flexibility) or fixed.
Choose card or sticker format based on placement environment. Counter card, table tent, checkout stand or peel-and-stick.
Match card design to brand: custom-printed cards outperform generic stickers for trust and tap rate.

brief.label: Chip silicon + form factor library
items: NTAG213 (144-byte) — baseline review-card silicon; rewritable URL; 90% of programme volume.
NTAG215 (504-byte) — premium card with photo / vCard hybrid + review URL.
NTAG 424 DNA — anti-clone / executive cards where review URL signing matters.
Standard PVC ID-1 0.76 mm — cheapest baseline + full CMYK / spot UV / foil.
Premium frosted / brushed PVC — visual upgrade for premium brands.
Tabletop tent / acrylic stand — passive-placement form for restaurant + waiting-room.
Counter card — vertical card with stand; payment-counter format.
Peel-and-stick NFC sticker — flexible deployment on any surface.
Receipt insert card — small format included with paper receipt.
Staff-carried lanyard card — clinic / home-service rep workflow.

brief.label: FTC + Google compliance framework
items: FTC 16 CFR Part 465 Rule on the Use of Consumer Reviews and Testimonials — effective Oct 21, 2024.
Federal rule prohibiting fake, AI-generated, insider, paid-for-positive, hidden-negative reviews.
FTC Endorsement Guides — material-connection disclosure for incentivised reviews.
Google Business Profile Review Policy — prohibits review-gating (only-positive-customers asked).
Card copy must say 'Leave us a review' — never 'Leave us a 5-star review'.
Cards must be offered to ALL customers (positive + negative) — not selectively to satisfied only.
No incentivisation: no discount + no entry-to-prize-draw + no free item for review.
EU Digital Services Act — obligates platforms to publish review-source transparency.
Australian ACCC + UK CMA — equivalent fake-review prohibition + enforcement.

brief.label: Multi-location encoding workflow
items: Google Business Profile per location — generate short review link per location URL.
Spreadsheet input: location name + address + review URL per row.
Production-stage encoding: each card encoded with location-specific URL.
Pre-sorted shipping: cards bundled by location for direct distribution.
Re-encoding: rewritable NTAG213 means future location changes (rebrand / relocation) just need NFC Tools rewrite.
Per-location analytics: GBP-side review velocity tracked per location.
Brand-standard governance: cohort decisions on chip / material / design / copy locked centrally.

brief.label: Tap-to-review UX flow
items: iPhone XS+ (iOS 14+): background tag reading enabled by default; tap top of phone → URL banner appears → tap to open.
iPhone 7 / 8 / X (iOS 11–13): NFC reading requires opening the Camera or NFC Tools app — fallback, not ideal.
Android (API 19+): native NDEF dispatch handler opens URL automatically on tap.
Read range typically 0–4 cm iPhone; 0–6 cm Android.
Logged-in Google account: review composer opens directly with star-selector.
Logged-out: prompt to sign in to Google before review submission.
QR fallback printed alongside NFC prompt — for phones with no NFC capability (very rare in 2026).

brief.label: Programme economics + ROI
items: Per-card BOM: $1.50–$3.50 PVC printed + NTAG213 at 50–500 qty; $0.80–$1.50 at 1k+ qty.
Per-location cost: typically $50–$200 covering 20–100 cards per location.
Review velocity uplift: 40–70% increase in monthly review volume vs verbal-only baseline.
Per-review acquisition cost: 80% reduction vs paid review-generation platforms ($0.50–$2 per review at scale).
Star-rating uplift: 4.2–4.4 → 4.6–4.8 typical within 3–4 months for businesses on consistent rollout.
Conversion uplift: businesses with ≥4.5 stars + ≥30 reviews convert 3–5× vs sub-30 review baselines.
Reorder cycle: 12–18 months typical; brand-refresh trigger or new-location rollout.
Replacement reserve: 5–10% per year for damaged / lost cards.

brief.label: Staff prompt + soft-skill playbook
items: Train staff on consistent verbal prompt: 'If you enjoyed your visit, would you mind tapping this card to leave us a Google review?'
Avoid loaded language: never ask for '5 stars' specifically — violates Google policy.
Time the prompt to peak satisfaction moment: end of meal, post-service, checkout.
Hand the card directly: physical handoff converts 3–5× higher than counter-passive placement.
Reciprocity: staff who provide excellent service earn the right to ask; coach team on service-then-prompt sequencing.
Track per-staff prompt completion rate as KPI; recognise consistent prompters.
Avoid pressure: customer can always decline; respect disengagement signals.

sections.title: Problems businesses face getting Google reviews without NFC cards
sections.intro: The review gap is almost always a friction gap. Customers who would review if asked directly don't follow through when the path from intent to posted review has more than two steps.

before: Verbal-only prompts at checkout — staff feel awkward; prompt happens inconsistently.
QR stand requires camera open + frame + scan + wait — 3-step friction at peak satisfaction moment.
Generic 'find us on Google' business card — drives no measurable uplift.
Multi-location: same card across all sites = reviews go to wrong location.
Customer intent decays from satisfaction moment to home — most reviews never posted.
No analytics on prompt-to-review conversion per location / per staff member.
after: Tap-to-review NFC card — single-gesture action at peak satisfaction moment.
iPhone XS+ background tag reading + Android NDEF dispatch — opens GBP review composer in 1 tap.
Custom-printed card with brand colours + logo + 'Tap to review' CTA — increases tap confidence.
Multi-location: per-location encoded card; reviews route to correct GBP automatically.
Captured at-the-moment of satisfaction — no decay window.
GBP-side analytics + staff-prompt KPI tracking provide complete review-funnel visibility.

bullets: Verbal review requests generate low conversion. Customers intend to review later, then forget by the time they reach their phone at home.
Printed QR stands require customers to open the camera, frame the code, and wait for a link — 3 steps vs 1 tap.
Business cards with 'find us on Google' drive no measurable review increase because customers don't act without a direct link.
Staff hesitancy: team members feel awkward asking verbally for reviews, so the prompt happens inconsistently or not at all.
Multi-location businesses struggle to route each location's card to the correct Google Business Profile. One wrong link means reviews go to the wrong location.

sections.title: How Proud Tek Google review NFC cards solve the friction problem
sections.intro: The solution is a single-tap action that opens the Google review composer directly. No camera, no search, no app. Proud Tek cards add custom branding and rewritable NFC to give businesses full control.
bullets: 3-second tap-to-review: customer taps card with any NFC-enabled iPhone (iPhone 7+) or Android phone. The Google review page opens immediately, no app required.
Custom-printed cards with brand colours, logo and a clear call to action increase perceived legitimacy and tap confidence versus generic white stickers.
NTAG213 chip with rewritable URL: if the business changes location, rebrands or switches to a different review platform, the NFC URL can be updated without reprinting the card.
Location-specific encoding: multi-location businesses get cards individually encoded to each location's Google Business Profile review link. No manual card sorting required.
Cards can include a QR code as a fallback for older phones, printed alongside the NFC prompt so no customer is excluded.

sections.title: Results: review volume impact from NFC tap cards
sections.intro: These figures are drawn from operator conversations and publicly referenced case studies. Outcomes vary by industry, placement quality and staff engagement.
bullets: Restaurants using counter tap cards report 50–70% more monthly Google reviews compared to verbal-only prompting.
Salons and beauty businesses see conversion rates of 15–30% on cards handed directly to customers at checkout versus under 5% for generic verbal requests.
Businesses with 4.2–4.4 star averages report that consistent review volume from NFC cards pushes ratings to 4.6–4.8 within 3–4 months of deployment.
Multi-location restaurant groups reduced per-review acquisition cost by 80% compared to paid review-generation platforms after switching to tap cards.
Clinics and dental practices report that post-appointment tap cards generate 3–5x more reviews than email follow-up campaigns.

dataHighlight.heading: Review-velocity uplift across 8 verticals post-NFC-card deployment
dataHighlight.text: Restaurants, cafes, clinics, dental practices, salons, spas, hotels, gyms, retail counters and home-services businesses consistently report 40–70 % monthly Google review velocity uplift after switching from verbal-only or QR-stand prompting to tap-to-review NFC cards. Conversion rates at point of handoff land at 15–30 % when staff hand cards directly with verbal prompt, vs sub-5 % for generic verbal requests alone. Star-rating uplift typically follows: 4.2–4.4 baseline → 4.6–4.8 within 3–4 months for businesses on consistent rollout. Per-review acquisition cost drops 80 % vs paid review-generation platforms ($0.50–$2 per review at scale). Programme economics: $1.50–$3.50 per card at 50–500 qty + 12–18 month reorder cycle + 5–10 % annual replacement reserve. FTC 16 CFR Part 465 + FTC Endorsement Guides + Google Business Profile review policies frame the operating envelope (no review-gating, no incentivisation, 'leave us a review' not '5-star review' copy).

items.label: Week 1 — GBP audit + per-location review-link capture
items.text: Verify Google Business Profile is claimed + verified for each location. Generate short review URL per location via 'Ask for reviews' workflow. Build spreadsheet: location name + address + GBP review URL per row.

items.label: Week 2 — Card design + chip selection + copy review
items.text: Brand colours + logo + clear CTA ('Tap here to leave a review'). Avoid '5-star' language. Choose chip: NTAG213 baseline, NTAG215 for premium card, NTAG 424 DNA for anti-clone executive cards. Choose form factor: counter card / table tent / staff-carried / sticker / receipt insert.

items.label: Week 3 — FTC + Google compliance review
items.text: Validate copy against FTC 16 CFR Part 465 + Google Business Profile review policy. Confirm no review-gating language. Confirm no incentivisation. Confirm 'leave us a review' (not '5-star review'). Sign off legal review.

items.label: Week 4 — Production + per-location encoding
items.text: Production wave on confirmed chip + design. Each card encoded with location-specific GBP URL. Pre-sorted shipping by location. Receiving QC: tap-test 5 % per batch + visual inspection.

items.label: Week 5–6 — Staff training + soft-launch
items.text: Train staff on consistent verbal prompt + handoff timing + soft-skill protocol. Soft-launch one location first; monitor staff-prompt completion rate + customer reception. Iterate on placement + copy if needed.

items.label: Month 2 — Full rollout + GBP analytics tracking
items.text: Roll out to all locations. Track per-location review velocity + star-rating trend in GBP analytics. Monitor staff-prompt KPI (% of customers offered card).

items.label: Month 3–6 — Optimise + reorder cycle
items.text: First quarterly review velocity assessment. Identify high-performing locations + best-practice patterns. Replace damaged / lost cards. Adjust placement + copy based on data. Confirm star-rating trend toward 4.6–4.8 target.

items.label: Year 2+ — Operate + brand-refresh + scale
items.text: Buyer-side operating notes for hospitality, healthcare, retail, fitness and home-services teams — each estate sets its own reorder cycle, FTC + Google compliance audit cadence and staff-prompt KPI scorecards. Reorder synced to brand-refresh trigger or new-location rollout (typical 12–18 month cycle). Multi-location estate scale-up + per-location compliance audit + per-staff recognition for consistent prompting.

faq.question: Do customers need an app to use a Google review NFC card?
faq.answer: No. Any NFC-enabled iPhone (iPhone 7 or later running iOS 14+) or Android phone can tap the card and open the Google review page directly in the browser. No app download is required. The NTAG213 chip used in Proud Tek cards is compatible with all mainstream NFC-enabled smartphones.

faq.question: How do I get my Google Business Profile review link?
faq.answer: Log into Google Business Profile, select your location, click 'Ask for reviews' and copy the short review link. This is the URL that gets programmed into the NFC chip. Make sure the link opens correctly on a mobile browser before sending it for card production.

faq.question: Can I update the NFC URL after the cards are printed?
faq.answer: Yes. Proud Tek cards use an NTAG213 chip with a rewritable URL by default. You can reprogram the destination using any NFC-capable phone and a free app such as NFC Tools. If you prefer cards to be locked permanently to a single URL, this is also available. Specify at order.

faq.question: What is the minimum order quantity for Google review NFC cards?
faq.answer: Sample orders start from 10–25 cards for design validation. Production runs typically start from 50–100 cards for single-location businesses. Multi-location orders with location-specific encoding start from 25 cards per location.

faq.question: Are NFC review cards better than QR review stands?
faq.answer: NFC cards produce faster action at the point of service because the tap is a single gesture. QR stands work better in environments where customers are seated and have time to frame and scan. The placement guide covers the conditions where each format performs best. Many businesses use both.

faq.question: How do multi-location businesses manage different review links?
faq.answer: Each location's cards are encoded to that location's individual Google Business Profile review link during production. Proud Tek handles per-location encoding from a spreadsheet of review links. You do not need to handle individual card programming. Cards are shipped pre-sorted by location.

faq.question: What card design works best for review prompts?
faq.answer: Cards with a clear call to action ('Tap to leave a review'), a recognisable Google logo or star graphic, and brand colours consistently outperform generic white or minimal designs. The design and copy guide covers the specific elements that affect tap rate and customer confidence.
